title: Attention Is All You Need
abstract: We propose the Transformer, a sequence model based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions.

title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
abstract: We introduce BERT, a new language representation model designed to pre-train deep bidirectional representations from unlabeled text.

title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
abstract: We demonstrate that scaling autoregressive language models yields strong few-shot performance across many tasks without gradient updates.

title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
abstract: We present residual networks, enabling the training of substantially deeper neural networks by learning residual functions.

title: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization
abstract: We introduce Adam, an algorithm for first-order gradient-based optimization of stochastic objective functions.

title: Batch Normalization: Accelerating Deep Network Training by Reducing Internal Covariate Shift
abstract: We propose Batch Normalization to reduce internal covariate shift, allowing higher learning rates and improving regularization.

title: A Survey on Graph Neural Networks
abstract: We review graph neural network models, architectures, and applications, and discuss open challenges for future research.
venue: IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems

title: RoBERTa: A Robustly Optimized BERT Pretraining Approach
abstract: We show that BERT was significantly undertrained and propose RoBERTa with improved training, data, and hyperparameters.

title: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
abstract: We present diffusion probabilistic models, a class of latent variable models that achieve high-quality image synthesis via denoising steps.

title: Federated Learning: Challenges, Methods, and Future Directions
abstract: We survey federated learning systems and algorithms, covering privacy, communication efficiency, and deployment challenges.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
abstract: We augment generation with neural retrieval to ground outputs in external documents and improve factuality on knowledge-intensive tasks.

title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
abstract: We propose LoRA, which injects trainable low-rank matrices into frozen weights, enabling efficient fine-tuning with fewer parameters.

title: Improving Language Understanding by Generative Pre-Training
abstract: We present a generative pre-training approach for language understanding, demonstrating transfer across tasks after unsupervised training.

title: Fast R-CNN
abstract: We propose Fast R-CNN, a method that speeds up training and improves detection accuracy via a single-stage training pipeline.

title: Mask R-CNN
abstract: We present a framework for object instance segmentation that extends Faster R-CNN by adding a branch for predicting segmentation masks.

title: U-Net: Convolutional Networks for Biomedical Image Segmentation
abstract: We propose U-Net, a convolutional network architecture for fast and precise segmentation of biomedical images from few annotated samples.

title: YOLOv3: An Incremental Improvement
abstract: We present improvements to YOLO, including multi-scale predictions and a better backbone, yielding strong real-time detection performance.

title: The Lottery Ticket Hypothesis: Finding Sparse, Trainable Neural Networks
abstract: We show that dense networks contain sparse subnetworks that can be trained in isolation to match test accuracy when initialized appropriately.

title: On the Opportunities and Risks of Foundation Models
abstract: We discuss capabilities, risks, and governance considerations for foundation models, and propose a taxonomy for evaluation and accountability.

title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
abstract: We show that prompting with chain-of-thought exemplars significantly improves reasoning performance on arithmetic, commonsense, and symbolic tasks.

title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
abstract: We study how performance scales with model size, dataset size, and compute, finding predictable power-law relationships useful for planning.

title: DistilBERT, a distilled version of BERT: smaller, faster, cheaper and lighter
abstract: We distill BERT into a smaller model retaining most of its language understanding while being faster and lighter for deployment.

title: ALBERT: A Lite BERT for Self-supervised Learning of Language Representations
abstract: We propose ALBERT with parameter reduction techniques and a sentence-order prediction objective to improve efficiency and performance.

title: Improved Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
abstract: We improve diffusion models with a hybrid objective, classifier-free guidance analysis, and architectural tweaks for better sample quality.

title: Self-Training Improves Neural Machine Translation
abstract: We show that noisy self-training with synthetic data can substantially improve neural machine translation quality in low-resource settings.

title: Longformer: The Long-Document Transformer
abstract: We introduce Longformer with an attention mechanism that scales linearly with sequence length, enabling processing of long documents.

title: What Does BERT Look at? An Analysis of BERT’s Attention
abstract: We analyze attention patterns in BERT and show that many heads capture linguistic phenomena, while others behave like positional or delimiter features.

title: Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code
abstract: We evaluate transformer-based language models on code generation and completion benchmarks, analyzing data contamination and generalization.

title: The Hardware Lottery
abstract: We argue that research progress is shaped by hardware and software constraints, and that 'winners' often align with available compute primitives.

title: A Survey of Hallucination in Large Language Models
abstract: We survey hallucination types in LLMs and mitigation strategies, including retrieval grounding, verification, and training-time interventions.

title: Textbooks Are All You Need II: Phi-1.5 Technical Report
abstract: We describe Phi-1.5, a small language model trained on high-quality synthetic and textbook-like data, and evaluate it on reasoning and coding tasks.

title: The NIST Definition of Cloud Computing
abstract: This document provides a definition of cloud computing and describes its essential characteristics, service models, and deployment models.

title: Sparks of Artificial General Intelligence: Early experiments with GPT-4
abstract: We report early experiments suggesting broad capabilities of GPT-4 across domains, and discuss limitations, safety, and evaluation challenges.

title: A Guide to Responsible AI Governance
abstract: We outline operational practices for responsible AI governance, including model documentation, risk assessment, monitoring, and incident response.

title: A Simple Baseline for Bayesian Uncertainty in Deep Learning
abstract: We present a practical baseline for predictive uncertainty using deep ensembles, and compare against dropout-based approximations on vision tasks.

title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
abstract: We introduce ReAct, interleaving reasoning traces and actions to improve performance on interactive tasks like question answering and web navigation.
